frontmatter.description: Checked four-qubit QAOA and two-qubit VQE examples, with complete optimization traces and separate sampled readout.

children.value: QAOA alternates an objective-dependent phase with a mixer, while VQE changes a trial state to reduce its energy

. Both are hybrid workflows: classical parameter search and repeated state preparations needed to evaluate an objective belong to the algorithm. Here we make those operations inspectable on two small problems.
The first examples on this page use explicit Qiskit circuits, exact statevector objectives, independent classical references, and separately seeded final-readout experiments. The

adds parameter updates driven by sampled objectives on the same tasks. The downloadable traces record every objective evaluation and all shot use. They check these particular circuits and runs; they establish no large-instance convergence guarantee or quantum advantage.

Logical workload and the pending physical handoff

children.label: Logical workload and the pending physical handoff

children.value: accompanies actual measured OpenQASM 3 circuits. It records gate counts, depth, width, input preparation, all sampling repetitions, basis changes, and readout. The graph is a classical edge list and the Hamiltonian is three explicit Pauli terms; no data-loading oracle is assumed. Classical input parsing, physical reset and measurement time, and device routing are excluded. Reference calculations are included in the whole CPU workflow timer, but their separate time is unmeasured.

The first demonstrated workload contains six exact classical optimization runs with their entire evaluation traces, plus three seeded readout experiments for each primary state. The ideal readout protocol represents 6,144 four-qubit QAOA preparations and 12,288 two-qubit VQE preparations, including both measurement bases. The generated ledger weights the explicit circuits by these shot counts; the samples themselves are drawn classically from statevector probabilities. Exact optimization evaluations use zero shots. The

provides a separate measured trace and shot allocation for every sampled training call. Multiplying one final circuit by an optimizer iteration count would not establish that workload’s convergence or accuracy.
The elementary exports retain H, CX, and one-qubit rotations. Arbitrary-angle RX, RY, and RZ gates are

synthesized into Clifford+T. The inputs support a later synthesis audit, but supply no validated T count, code distance, factory allocation, physical-qubit count, or quantum runtime. Coherent rotation approximation error and stochastic fault probability need separate budgets before a surface-code comparison. The existing

The QAOA generator accepts a supplied graph and layer angles; the VQE generator exposes its ansatz parameter. Materialization is capped at 100,000 unitary gates before optional final measurements; the ledger includes those measurements. QAOA exact statevector simulation defaults to a small configured bound with a hard cap of 16 qubits; exhaustive enumeration has its own hard cap of 20. Circuit export is separate from these classical computations. Larger exports do not imply affordable simulation or project the number of optimization evaluations needed at larger sizes.

The original exact workflow has 40 dedicated checks. Additional sampled, projection, replay and second-instance checks exercise the extended workflows; each notebook is freshly executed before publication. QAOA is checked against exhaustive classical cut enumeration and independently assembled dense evolution, including asymmetric multiple-layer angles. Tests verify cost signs, angle conventions, bit ordering and complete evaluation traces.

The two-qubit VQE example is checked against the full Hamiltonian spectrum and an independent analytic energy expression. Its ansatz contains this particular toy ground state; that does not imply general VQE expressibility or convergence. All optimizer starts, rejected proposals, stopping conditions and objective calls are recorded.

Readout tests retain the covariance of jointly measured Z terms, independent X/Z streams, reproducible counts, bounded-outcome Hoeffding calculations and shot-weighted gate totals. Sample standard errors are descriptive; the stated ideal bounds are per fixed estimate, not simultaneous guarantees across every seed or optimizer parameter.

The chapter explicitly distinguishes exact-statevector optimization from ideal sampled final validation. Actual ideal finite-shot trajectories are now recorded. Conditional projections replay their fixed measured paths; a hardware/noisy optimizer trajectory, certified synthesis and formal proof remain unestablished. A separate 32-qubit generation run verifies export/counts without simulation or optimization.
